IR.rationale: A rise in the 5-year yield relative to the policy rate marks a repricing of the expected rate path and term premium at the belly of the curve, which drives bond index returns. Bond excess returns show both short-run continuation and reversal of such moves.

B.rationale: Widening corporate spreads together with weak high-yield returns signal credit stress. Credit stress triggers flight-to-quality demand for Treasuries and pushes down risk-free yields.

V.rationale: High equity implied volatility proxies risk aversion and safe-haven demand. That demand supports Treasury prices and tends to precede accommodative policy expectations.

AP.rationale: In the low-inflation regime the stock-bond correlation is negative. Weak equity returns therefore coincide with, and can lead, falling yields and positive bond returns.

ST.rationale: Equity cross-sectional style factors have no clear mechanism linking them to Treasury or investment-grade bond returns beyond what the market factor captures.

FX.rationale: Yen appreciation is a classic risk-off and carry-unwind signal. It coincides with global demand for safe government bonds.

COM.rationale: Rising broad commodity prices feed inflation expectations and push up nominal yields, which lowers nominal bond returns. Inflation-linked bonds are partly shielded from this effect.

MC.rationale: Rising breakeven inflation raises nominal yields through the inflation-compensation component, so it maps directly into bond returns. The sign of the effect differs for inflation-linked indices.

ENDG.rationale: Government bond indices exhibit time-series momentum over weeks to months, so recent strong returns carry information about subsequent returns.

IR.rationale: A simultaneous hawkish repricing of the front end and the belly relative to the policy rate signals monetary policy uncertainty. Such uncertainty raises subsequent rate volatility beyond its own persistence.

B.rationale: Widening credit spreads indicate deteriorating risk appetite. This is followed by turbulent flight-to-quality flows and larger moves in Treasury and corporate bond prices.

V.rationale: Elevated equity implied volatility combined with high policy uncertainty captures a broad uncertainty state. Interest-rate volatility co-moves with that state and lags it.

AP.rationale: Equity sell-offs raise volatility asymmetrically, and the effect spills into bond markets through rebalancing and safe-haven flows.

ST.rationale: No well-documented link exists between equity style factors and bond index variance.

FX.rationale: Sharp dollar appreciation reflects global funding stress or diverging policy expectations, both of which are associated with higher volatility in US rates.

COM.rationale: Commodity price collapses are disinflationary and growth shocks. They prompt large repricings of inflation compensation and the expected policy path, especially in inflation-linked bonds.

MC.rationale: The financial stress index aggregates funding, credit and bond-market volatility measures. High stress forecasts elevated subsequent bond market variance.

ENDG.rationale: Bond variance clusters and mean-reverts, so the recent level relative to its history helps correct the persistence already built into the baseline.

IR.rationale: Rising intermediate yields together with a steepening curve describe a bear-steepening sell-off driven by term premium. This is the state in which duration losses become large and self-reinforcing.

B.rationale: Tightening spreads and strong high-yield returns mark a risk-on regime. In that regime safe-haven demand for Treasuries fades and yields can jump.

V.rationale: Low risk aversion removes the flight-to-quality bid. This leaves bonds exposed to rate repricing driven by growth or policy.

AP.rationale: Strong equity rallies, under a negative stock-bond correlation, accompany rising yields and portfolio outflows from bonds.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors carry no clear information about bond tail losses.

FX.rationale: Yen weakness signals risk-on carry positioning, which coincides with selling of safe-haven bonds.

COM.rationale: Commodity price surges raise inflation risk and expected policy tightening, a key driver of large losses in nominal bonds.

MC.rationale: Rising inflation expectations under loose financial conditions describe a reflationary state that invites tighter policy. That combination produces outsized yield increases.

ENDG.rationale: Weak recent bond returns tend to continue at short horizons, through time-series momentum and the deleveraging of duration positions.

IR.rationale: Falling bill rates together with falling intermediate yields relative to the policy rate indicate a dovish repricing of the policy path. That repricing produces large duration gains.

B.rationale: Credit stress drives flight-to-quality into Treasuries, generating large rallies in government bond indices.

V.rationale: Spikes in risk aversion are when safe-haven demand and expectations of policy easing deliver outsized bond gains.

AP.rationale: Equity sell-offs coincide with strong bond rallies under a negative stock-bond correlation.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors offer no documented mechanism for bond tail gains.

FX.rationale: Yen appreciation signals global risk-off and carry unwinds, which accompany strong demand for government bonds.

COM.rationale: Oil price declines lower inflation expectations and signal weaker growth, supporting large declines in yields.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress triggers safe-haven flows and expectations of policy easing, both conducive to large bond gains.

ENDG.rationale: Bond return momentum makes strong recent returns informative about the chance of continued large gains.
